verdict.summary:
ANSWERS (Approved Document B, Fire safety, Volume 1: Dwellings, 2019 edition incorporating the 2020, 2022, 2025 and 2026 amendments — England)

(a) Sprinklers throughout: blocks of flats with a top storey MORE THAN 11 m above ground level (paragraph 7.4).
(b) Trigger height before the 2020 amendments: MORE THAN 30 m above ground level (i.e. a reduction from 30 m to 11 m).
(c) More than one common stair: blocks of flats with a storey 18 m OR MORE in height (new recommendation introduced by the 2026 amendments), taking effect 30 SEPTEMBER 2026 for use in England.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
1. SCOPE / PROVENANCE (Ask 1 — constraint)
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
All figures below are taken from the current consolidated ADB Volume 1 for England, i.e. the 2019 edition incorporating the 2020, 2022, 2025 and 2026 amendments (the online PDF also carries the forthcoming 2029 changes, which are not yet in force).

Sources used:
- ADB Vol 1, 2019 edition incorporating 2020, 2022, 2025 and 2026 amendments (current online version): https://assets.publishing.service.gov.uk/media/6aa3bb335f6e942efe37f150/AD_B1_2026.pdf — front matter, 'Main changes made by the 2020 / 2022 / 2025 / 2026 / 2029 amendments'.
- ADB Vol 1, 2019 edition incorporating 2020 and 2022 amendments: https://assets.publishing.service.gov.uk/media/67d02386f5aaff610c9f5f06/...pdf — same 'Main changes' front matter.
- ADB 2019 edition, May 2020 amendments booklet: https://assets.publishing.service.gov.uk/media/5ec7f1c086650c76ab17fc0c/AD_B_2019_edition__May2020_amendments.pdf — 'Section 7: Compartmentation/sprinklers – flats, Page 59 Replace paragraph 7.4 with the following…'.
- DLUHC/Building Safety circular letter of 26 May 2020: https://assets.publishing.service.gov.uk/government/uploads/system/uploads/attachment_data/file/924446/...pdf — 'A reduction in the trigger height from 30m to 11m'; transitional date 26 November 2020.
- ADB 2026 amendments booklet: https://assets.publishing.service.gov.uk/media/66d57a94d107658faec7e448/AD_B_2026_amendments.pdf — 'Taking effect on 30 September 2026'; 'Section 3: Means of escape – flats … Replace paragraph 3.27'.
- GOV.UK amendments circular/letter (table of amendment booklets, content, coming into force, deposit periods): '2026 Approved Document B amendments booklet — Second stair provisions in residential buildings over 18m in height — 30 September 2026'.

Language convention throughout: ADB is APPROVED DOCUMENT guidance, not the legal requirement. The legal requirements are in the Building Regulations 2010 (Schedule 1, Part B, principally B1 means of escape, B3 internal fire spread (structure), B5 access and facilities for the fire service). 'Should' in ADB = the normal way to comply; a different approach is permissible if it satisfies the requirement (and, in practice, is accepted by building control / a registered building control approver).

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
2. ASK-BY-ASK, WITH THE GOVERNING TEXT
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

ASK 2 — Current sprinkler trigger height: 11 m (top storey MORE THAN 11 m above ground level)

May 2020 amendment booklet, List of amendments, Section 7: Compartmentation/sprinklers – flats, page 59, 'Replace paragraph 7.4 with the following':

  '7.4  Blocks of flats with a top storey more than 11m above ground level (see Diagram D6) should be fitted with a sprinkler system throughout the building in accordance with Appendix E.
   NOTE: Sprinklers should be provided within the individual flats, they do not need to be provided in the common areas such as stairs, corridors or landings when these areas are fire sterile.'

This is the text carried into the current consolidated volume. Two practical points that follow directly from the quoted wording:
- 'Throughout the building' is qualified by the NOTE: full provision within every flat; common areas (stairs, corridors, landings) may be omitted where they are fire sterile. So 'throughout' does not mean a head in every stair enclosure.
- The system standard is Appendix E: BS 9251 for residential blocks of flats within its scope, BS EN 12845 for residential blocks of flats outside the scope of BS 9251. The May 2020 circular letter confirms Appendix E was NOT changed: 'There are no changes to Appendix E which will continue to recommend that sprinkler systems in residential blocks of flats are installed in accordance with the recommendations of BS 9251, or BS EN 12845 for residential blocks of flats outside of the scope of BS 9251.'

Semantics: the threshold is EXCLUSIVE — 'more than 11m'. A top storey at exactly 11.00 m does not trigger paragraph 7.4 (though it does trigger other 11 m provisions: Section 10 external-wall provisions for purpose groups 1 and 2 with a storey 11 m or more, wayfinding signage for storeys over 11 m, and the Table B4 fire-resistance adjustments).

ASK 3 — Trigger height before the 2020 amendments: 30 m (top storey MORE THAN 30 m above ground level)

May 2020 amendment booklet, 'Main changes made by the 2020 amendments':
  'a. Sprinklers: A reduction in the trigger height from 30m to 11m.'

Repeated verbatim in the front matter of the current consolidated volume and in the 26 May 2020 circular letter ('The amendments include a reduction in the height threshold for sprinklers in Purpose group…').

Because the 2020 booklet's instruction is 'Replace paragraph 7.4 with the following' and the replacement is the 11 m text above, the pre-amendment paragraph 7.4 was the same sentence with '30m' in place of '11m' — i.e. 'Blocks of flats with a top storey more than 30m above ground level (see Diagram D6) should be fitted with a sprinkler system throughout the building in accordance with Appendix E.' That 30 m figure is the 2019-edition position and traces back to the 2006/2010-era ADB. (If a verbatim pre-2020 quotation is needed for a report, cite the 2019 edition as originally published, read with the May 2020 amendment booklet; the booklet is the authoritative statement that the old figure was 30 m.)

For completeness on dates in this round (not asked, but commonly conflated): the 2020 changes took effect on 26 NOVEMBER 2020, with the 2019 edition continuing to apply where a building notice or initial notice had been given, or full plans deposited, before 26 November 2020 and the work had started before that day or started before 29 January 2021.

ASK 4 — More than one common stair: 18 m (a storey 18 m OR MORE in height)

Current consolidated volume, 'Main changes made by the 2026 amendments':
  'a. A new recommendation for more than one common stair to be provided in blocks of flats with a storey 18m or more in height.
   b. Building design provisions to support the use of evacuation lifts in blocks of flats.'

2026 amendments booklet, Section 3: Means of escape – flats, 'Means of escape in the common parts of flats': 'Page 26 Replace subheading "Number of escape routes" with the following. Design for horizontal escape. Replace paragraph 3.27 with the following. 3.27 From the flat entrance door, a single escape route is acceptable in either of the following cases. a. The flat is on a storey served by a single common stair and both of the following apply. i. Every flat is separated from the common stair by a protected lobby or common protected corridor (see Diagram 3.7)…'

So the 2026 amendments restructure the 'number of escape routes' guidance into 'design for horizontal escape', and a single common stair is retained as acceptable only within the stated conditions and below the 18 m threshold; at 18 m or above, the recommendation is more than one common stair.

Two precision points a fire engineer must not blur:
- The wording is 'a storey 18m or more in height' — INCLUSIVE at 18.00 m, and expressed on 'a storey' rather than 'top storey more than'. Compare the sprinkler paragraph, which is 'top storey more than 11m' — EXCLUSIVE at 11.00 m. Do not carry the sprinkler grammar across to the stair threshold.
- It is a recommendation in guidance ('should'), delivered through the means-of-escape provisions, and it sits alongside the new evacuation-lift design provisions. It does not by itself create a statutory duty; compliance with B1 remains the legal test.

ASK 5 — Effective date of the second-stair changes: 30 September 2026

2026 amendments booklet cover: 'Taking effect on 30 September 2026'.
2026 amendments booklet, transitional text: 'The changes highlighted in this amendment booklet take effect on 30 September 2026 for use in England. The 2019 edition incorporating the 2020, 2022 and 2025 amendments will continue to apply where a building notice or an initial notice has been given to, or a building control approval application with full plans made to, the relevant authority before 30 September 2026 and either the building work to which it relates: a. has started and is sufficiently progressed before that day; or b. …'
GOV.UK amendment table: '2026 Approved Document B amendments booklet | Second stair provisions in residential buildings over 18m in height | 30 September 2026 | Amending Approved Document B 2019 incorporating the 2020, 2022 and 2025 amendments | 18 months' (the last column is the period to deposit an application).

Transitional consequence to state on any project: for work where a building notice / initial notice was given, or full plans deposited, before 30 September 2026 and the work started (and is sufficiently progressed) within the transitional window, the 2019 edition incorporating the 2020, 2022 and 2025 amendments continues to apply — i.e. the second-stair recommendation does NOT bite, and the 11 m sprinkler threshold does. Read the booklet's full transitional paragraph for the exact wording of limb (b) and the 18-month deposit period.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
3. WHAT DID *NOT* CHANGE (guards against the wrong-amendment error)
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
- 2020 amendments: sprinkler trigger 30 m → 11 m; new fire-service wayfinding signage for storeys over 11 m; Table B4 adjusted to reflect that a block of flats above 11 m without sprinklers is not permitted if following the guidance; Appendix E unchanged (BS 9251 / BS EN 12845). Effective 26 November 2020.
- 2022 amendments: combustible-materials ban consequences (Building (Amendment) (England) Regulations 2022), Section 10 provisions for purpose groups 1 and 2 with a storey 11 m or more; secure information boxes. No change to the 11 m sprinkler trigger or to the number of stairs.
- 2025 amendments: Regulation 38 / fire safety information; removal of national (BS 476) classes for reaction to fire and roofs; sprinklers in care homes. Effective 2 March 2025. No change to the 11 m sprinkler trigger for flats and no second-stair provision.
- 2026 amendments: second stair at 18 m or more; evacuation-lift design provisions. Effective 30 September 2026.
- 2029 amendments (present in the current PDF but NOT yet in force): removal of national (BS 476) classes for fire resistance; effective 2 September 2029. These do not change either threshold — do not answer Ask 5 with 2 September 2029.

Therefore, 'as currently published' (2019 + 2020 + 2022 + 2025 + 2026): sprinklers at top storey more than 11 m; second stair at a storey 18 m or more; second-stair effective date 30 September 2026.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
4. HOW TO APPLY THE TWO THRESHOLDS TOGETHER (worked outcomes)
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Take 'height' as the height above ground level of the relevant storey, measured per Diagram D6, to which paragraph 7.4 cross-refers (in practice the floor level of the top storey; confirm the convention on Diagram D6 where site levels step, or where the topmost storey is a roof/plant storey — ADB's defined 'top storey' excludes a storey consisting exclusively of plant or machinery).

- Top storey floor 10.0 m: no sprinkler trigger under 7.4; single common stair acceptable (subject to the paragraph 3.27 conditions).
- Top storey floor exactly 11.0 m: 7.4 not triggered ('more than 11m'); the 11 m provisions in Section 10 / wayfinding / Table B4 still apply; single common stair acceptable.
- Top storey floor 11.5 m: sprinklers throughout the flats required (11.5 > 11); single common stair still acceptable (11.5 < 18).
- Storey at exactly 18.0 m: second-stair recommendation engaged (18 m or more, inclusive); sprinklers required.
- Storey 24 m: sprinklers required; more than one common stair recommended.
So the band 11 m < h < 18 m is the 'sprinklers but one stair' band, and the deliverable must not present 18 m as if it were the sprinkler threshold or 11 m as if it were the stair threshold.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
5. CAVEATS / THINGS TO VERIFY BEFORE ISSUE
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
1. This is England only. Wales, Scotland and Northern Ireland have their own documents and thresholds; do not export these figures. (Wales in particular diverges on sprinklers in dwellings.)
2. Check the revision date of the online PDF at the moment of issue; the current file also carries the 2029 changes, which are not in force until 2 September 2029.
3. For a specific project, establish the transitional position first: whether the building notice / initial notice / full-plans deposit pre-dates 26 November 2020 (sprinkler 30 m may still govern) and/or 30 September 2026 (single stair may still be acceptable above 18 m), and whether work started within the relevant window.
4. Confirm the measurement convention against Diagram D6 and the volume's definition of 'top storey' where the topmost storey is plant or roof, and where ground levels vary around the building.
5. 'More than one common stair' is guidance delivered through means-of-escape provisions; the design justification (including any evacuation-lift strategy) must still demonstrate compliance with B1, and fire-engineered alternatives remain possible but carry the burden of proof with the approving authority.

verdict.summary:
MUTCD PEDESTRIAN INTERVAL VALUES — 11th Edition (Dec. 2023) vs. 2009 Edition

1. DIRECT ANSWERS

| # | Question | Answer | Status of the requirement | Citation |
|---|----------|--------|---------------------------|----------|
| 1 | Minimum buffer interval (steady UPRAISED HAND) after the pedestrian change interval, before release of a conflicting vehicular movement — MUTCD 11th Ed. (Dec. 2023) | 2 seconds (minimum, 'at least') | STANDARD ('shall') | MUTCD 11th Ed., Section 4I.06, Paragraph 04 (p. 722) |
| 2 | Default walking speed for sizing pedestrian clearance time | 3.5 feet per second | GUIDANCE ('should') | MUTCD 11th Ed., Section 4I.06, Paragraph 07 (p. 723) |
| 3 | Buffer interval minimum in the 2009 MUTCD | 3 seconds (minimum, 'at least') | STANDARD ('shall') | MUTCD 2009 Ed., Section 4E.06, Paragraph 04 |

Net change between editions: the buffer interval minimum was reduced from 3 seconds (2009) to 2 seconds (2023). The default walking speed of 3.5 ft/s is unchanged in substance between the two editions.

2. SOURCE TEXT (verbatim)

2.1 Ask 1 — 11th Edition, Section 4I.06, Paragraph 04 (Standard):
"A pedestrian change interval consisting of a flashing UPRAISED HAND (symbolizing DONT WALK) signal indication shall begin immediately following the WALKING PERSON (symbolizing WALK) signal indication. Following the pedestrian change interval, a buffer interval consisting of a steady UPRAISED HAND (symbolizing DONT WALK) signal indication shall be displayed for at least 2 seconds prior to the release of any conflicting vehicular movement. The sum of the time of the pedestrian change interval and the buffer interval shall not be less than the calculated pedestrian clearance time (see Paragraphs 7 through 16 of this Section). The buffer interval shall not begin later than the beginning of the red clearance interval, if used."

2.2 Ask 2 — 11th Edition, Section 4I.06, Paragraph 07 (Guidance):
"Except as provided in Paragraph 8 of this Section, the pedestrian clearance time should be sufficient to allow a pedestrian crossing in the crosswalk who left the curb or edge of pavement at the end of the WALKING PERSON (symbolizing WALK) signal indication to travel at a walking speed of 3.5 feet per second to at least the far side of the traveled way or to a median of sufficient width for pedestrians to wait."

2.3 Ask 3 — 2009 Edition, Section 4E.06, Paragraph 04 (Standard):
"A pedestrian change interval consisting of a flashing UPRAISED HAND (symbolizing DONT WALK) signal indication shall begin immediately following the WALKING PERSON (symbolizing WALK) signal indication. Following the pedestrian change interval, a buffer interval consisting of a steady UPRAISED HAND (symbolizing DONT WALK) signal indication shall be displayed for at least 3 seconds prior to the release of any conflicting vehicular movement. The sum of the time of the pedestrian change interval and the buffer interval shall not be less than the calculated pedestrian clearance time (see Paragraphs 7 through 16). The buffer interval shall not begin later than the beginning of the red clearance interval, if used."

3. QUALIFIERS ON THE 3.5 ft/s DEFAULT (do not misapply)

- 4 ft/s is NOT the default. 11th Ed. 4I.06 Paragraph 08 is an OPTION: "A walking speed of up to 4 feet per second may be used to evaluate the sufficiency of the pedestrian clearance time at locations where an extended push button press function has been installed to provide slower pedestrians" additional time. It applies only where that extended-pushbutton function exists; it is a permissive evaluation speed, not the sizing default.
- Slower than 3.5 ft/s is permitted where warranted. 11th Ed. 4I.06 Paragraph 10 (Guidance): "Where pedestrians who walk slower than 3.5 feet per second, or pedestrians who use wheelchairs, routinely use the crosswalk, a walking speed of less than 3.5 feet per second should be considered in determining the pedestrian clearance time." Common practice is 3.0 ft/s for such locations; the MUTCD states 'less than 3.5' without prescribing a single reduced value.
- The 2009 Edition used the same 3.5 ft/s baseline; its Paragraph 10 carried the identical 'slower than 3.5 feet per second' guidance language, confirming 3.5 ft/s as the default in both editions.
- Caution on a secondary source: the CDOT Guidelines for Pedestrian Signal Timing contains a typographical error reading 'a walking speed of up to 4 seconds'; the MUTCD text is 'up to 4 feet per second.' Do not propagate the '4 seconds' wording.

4. RELATED CONSTRAINTS THAT BOUND THE BUFFER INTERVAL (for applying Ask 1 correctly)

(a) Sum rule: pedestrian change interval + buffer interval >= calculated pedestrian clearance time. The buffer may be counted toward the calculated clearance time, or may begin after it has ended (11th Ed. Figure 4I-4, note ***: the Buffer Interval 'may be used to help satisfy the calculated pedestrian clearance time, or may begin after the calculated pedestrian clearance time has ended').
(b) Latest start: the buffer interval shall not begin later than the beginning of the red clearance interval, if used.
(c) The buffer interval shall always be provided and displayed (Figure 4I-4, note ***).
(d) Walk interval: should be at least 7 s (Guidance, Para 11); may be as short as 4 s where pedestrian volumes/characteristics do not require 7 s (Option, Para 12).
(e) Yellow change interval: at least 3 s (Figure 4I-4 legend).

5. WORKED TIMING EXAMPLE (compliant with 4(a)–(e) above)

Crosswalk: 60 ft from curb to far side of traveled way; no median; default 3.5 ft/s.
- Calculated pedestrian clearance time = 60 ft / 3.5 ft/s = 17.1 s.
- Select buffer interval = 2.0 s (the 11th Ed. minimum, Ask 1).
- Pedestrian change interval (flashing HAND, with countdown) = 17.1 - 2.0 = 15.1 s. Check sum rule: 15.1 + 2.0 = 17.1 s >= 17.1 s — satisfied.
- Walk interval = 7 s (Guidance minimum). Total pedestrian phase = 7 + 15.1 + 2.0 = 24.1 s.
- Buffer must terminate (i.e., conflicting vehicular green may be released) no earlier than the end of the 2.0 s steady HAND; the buffer may not begin later than the start of the red clearance interval if one is used. Under the 2009 Edition, the same geometry would have required a buffer of at least 3.0 s (flashing HAND 14.1 s + buffer 3.0 s = 17.1 s).

6. SCOPE NOTES / CAVEATS

- Values above are from the FHWA national MUTCD (11th Edition, December 2023, and 2009 Edition). State MUTCD supplements may amend these; e.g., state-specific editions can retain or modify paragraph text, so verify against the governing state manual before finalizing field timing.
- The 11th Edition figure/paragraph numbering differs from the 2009 Edition (4I.06 vs. 4E.06); citations above reflect each edition's own numbering, so the two numbers are not in conflict — they are different editions of the same requirement.
- The 2 s and 3 s values are minimums; longer buffer intervals are permitted and are often produced automatically where the buffer and the all-red interval terminate at the same time.

Combined Package and Port Group Current Limits
The 40 mA per-pin absolute maximum is a stress limit, not a guaranteed drive capability (output voltage is characterized at 20 mA and VCC = 5 V under the stated temperature conditions); total current through all VCC and GND pins must not exceed 200 mA. Additionally, Microchip enforces strict port group current limits: total steady-state sink current (IOL) must not exceed 100 mA each for (1) Ports C0-C5 + ADC6/ADC7, (2) Ports B0-B5 + D5-D7 + XTAL1/XTAL2, and (3) Ports D0-D4 + RESET. Total source current (IOH) must not exceed 150 mA each for (1) Ports C0-C5 + D0-D4 + ADC7 + RESET, and (2) Ports B0-B5 + D5-D7 + ADC6 + XTAL1/XTAL2.

verdict.summary:
# Thermal data for ATmega328P, 28-pin PDIP, per DS40002061B (09/2020)

## 1. Status of the two requested figures

**Ask 2 (theta-JA, 28-pin PDIP) — NOT ANSWERED. Blocked.**
**Ask 3 (max junction temperature or total power dissipation) — NOT ANSWERED. Blocked.**

Both are blocked for the same reason: the material actually retrieved for this task contains no thermal-characteristics content from DS40002061B. Specifically, what was retrieved was:

| Source | What it actually contains | Thermal data? |
|---|---|---|
| microchip.com/en-us/product/ATmega328P | Site navigation menus, chatbot widget text, footer | None |
| microchip.com/en-us/product/atmega48a, /atmega88pa | Same boilerplate; confirms the datasheet title "ATmega48A/PA/88A/PA/168A/PA/328/P Data Sheet" | None |
| Atmel-7810 Automotive ATmega328P datasheet (7810D) | Pin descriptions, data memory map, TWI state diagrams. Different document and different device grade from DS40002061B | None |
| Atmel-42735A ATmega328/P Datasheet Summary (06/2016) | Ordering information, package list, pin multiplexing, data retention. A 16-page summary; contains no electrical or thermal characteristics | None |
| datasheet.octopart.com (ATMEGA328P-MU) | Same 42735A summary content | None |
| circuitbase.tech/component/atmega328p | Third-party pinout page; states "Junction temperature -55 – 125 °C" and a 200 mA VCC/GND total | Third-party, not citable |

I will not emit a theta-JA number from memory. A thermal resistance is the input to a copper-area/heatsink/derating decision; a wrong or unattributed value here is worse than an explicit gap, and ask 1 constrains the answer to DS40002061B specifically. Substituting a figure from a generic PDIP-28 table, from the automotive 7810D datasheet, or from a distributor page would produce an answer that *looks* compliant with ask 1 while violating it.

## 2. What is verified, and can be used now

The package identification is confirmed from the ordering information in the retrieved summary (Atmel-42735A, section 3.2):

- Package code **28P3** = "28-lead, 0.300" Wide, Plastic Dual Inline Package (PDIP)".
- ATmega328P ordering codes in 28P3: **ATmega328P-PU** (industrial, -40 °C to +85 °C) and **ATmega328P-PN**.
- 28P3 is a 28-lead, 0.300 in (7.62 mm) body, 2.54 mm pitch through-hole package; it has no exposed thermal pad and no thermal vias, so its theta-JA is dominated by the lead frame and the board it is soldered into.

Any thermal figure must be matched on **both** device (ATmega328P, not 48A/88A/168A) and **package (28P3)**, because the datasheet covers four devices and four packages (28M1 QFN, 28P3 PDIP, 32M1-A QFN, 32A TQFP).

## 3. Extraction procedure — how to close asks 2 and 3 in one pass

Open DS40002061B and work through these locations in order. Record the result in the record template in section 4.

1. **Electrical Characteristics chapter, Absolute Maximum Ratings table** (near the end of the document, immediately before DC Characteristics). Read every line. The three possible outcomes for ask 3 are:
   - **(a)** A line reading "Junction temperature" or "Operating junction temperature" with min/max values → that is the ask-3 answer; take the maximum and its unit (°C).
   - **(b)** Only a line reading "Operating temperature ........ -55 °C to +125 °C" → the datasheet specifies **no** junction temperature and **no** total power dissipation. The honest ask-3 answer is then the literal statement "not specified; the Absolute Maximum Ratings give an operating temperature range of -55 °C to +125 °C", and the 125 °C top of that range is the value to carry into derating, flagged as an operating-temperature limit rather than a junction-temperature limit.
   - **(c)** A line reading "Total power dissipation" or "Power dissipation" with a per-package value (often with a derating factor in mW/°C above 25 °C) → that is the ask-3 answer; take the value and note the ambient condition it is quoted at.
2. **Search the whole PDF for the strings** `theta`, `JA`, `Thermal`, `junction`, `power dissipation`, `°C/W`. If a **Thermal Characteristics** table exists, it will be in or adjacent to the Electrical Characteristics chapter and will be a small table with one row per package.
3. **From that table, read the 28P3 / PDIP row only.** Record theta-JA, its unit (°C/W), and — critically — the test condition column. Thermal resistance without its condition is unusable. Expect one of: "still air, JEDEC 2-layer board", "still air, JEDEC 4-layer board", or a bare number with a footnote referencing a JEDEC JESD51 board.
4. **If no Thermal Characteristics table exists in the datasheet at all**, then the correct answer to ask 2 is "not specified in DS40002061B". In that case the only citable per-package theta-JA is Microchip's separate package thermal data (published per package code, 28P3), which is a *different document* and therefore does **not** satisfy ask 1's constraint — state it as a separate, clearly-labelled source.
5. **Cite page, table number and revision string** (`DS40002061B`, 09/2020) so the reader can verify. Do not accept a page number from a different revision.

## 4. Extraction record template (fill in on inspection)

```
Document        : Microchip DS40002061B, ATmega48A/PA/88A/PA/168A/PA/328/P Complete Datasheet, rev. 09/2020
Device          : ATmega328P
Package         : 28P3  (28-lead, 0.300 in PDIP; ordering codes -PU / -PN)

[ASK 2]
Parameter       : theta-JA, thermal resistance junction-to-ambient
Value           : ______  Unit: degC/W
Test condition  : ______ (still air / board type / airflow / footnote ref)
Location        : Section ____ , Table ____ , page ____

[ASK 3]
Parameter       : ( ) Maximum junction temperature  Tj,max   -> Value: ______ degC
                  ( ) Total power dissipation        Ptot     -> Value: ______ W  at TA = ______ degC
                  ( ) Neither tabulated; Absolute Maximum Ratings give only:
                      Operating temperature ______ degC to ______ degC
Location        : Section ____ , Table ____ , page ____
```

## 5. Interim thermal budget — explicitly NOT datasheet values

Until the table above is filled in, use this to keep a design moving. It is a bounding calculation, not a citation. Two inputs are deliberately conservative placeholders:

- **Tj,max = 125 °C** — the top of the industrial operating range and the conventional AVR limit. Confirm against section 3 outcome (a)/(b) before release.
- **theta-JA = 40 / 45 / 50 / 55 / 60 / 70 °C/W** — the generic band for a 28-lead 0.300 in PDIP on a JEDEC 2-layer board in still air. This is package-class data, **not** a DS40002061B figure, and must never be quoted as one.

Maximum allowable dissipation and the equivalent 5 V supply current:

| theta-JA (°C/W) | Ptot,max at TA = 85 °C (W) | Equivalent I at 5 V (mA) | Ptot,max at TA = 25 °C (W) |
|---|---|---|---|
| 40 | 1.000 | 200 | 2.500 |
| 45 | 0.889 | 178 | 2.222 |
| 50 | 0.800 | 160 | 2.000 |
| 55 | 0.727 | 145 | 1.818 |
| 60 | 0.667 | 133 | 1.667 |
| 70 | 0.571 | 114 | 1.429 |

(Computed as Ptot = (Tj,max - TA) / theta-JA with Tj,max = 125 °C; current = Ptot / 5 V.)

Two conclusions that hold for any theta-JA in this band and that a layout review should act on:

1. **At TA = 85 °C the PDIP is thermally limited at or below its own current rating.** At theta-JA = 40 °C/W the thermal ceiling (200 mA) exactly equals the 200 mA total VCC/GND absolute-maximum stress rating; at any higher theta-JA the thermal ceiling is lower. So the 200 mA figure is never a usable operating target in a hot enclosure — it is a stress limit only.
2. **At TA = 25 °C the current limit governs, not the package.** The thermal ceiling (e.g. 2.0 W at theta-JA = 50 °C/W) is above the 1.0 W implied by the 200 mA limit, so the current rating is the binding constraint there.

For the actual application current, the package is a non-issue: a 16 MHz, 5 V ATmega328P with peripherals at 15 mA total dissipates 75 mW, giving a rise of 75 mW x 50 °C/W = **3.75 °C** — negligible. theta-JA for the 28P3 matters only if the design drives sustained I/O current near the port-group and total-VCC/GND limits, which is the case to check at layout review.

## 6. Notes for whoever applies this

- Do not mix revisions. DS40002061B (09/2020) is the cited source; older Atmel-branded revisions (e.g. 8271, 2545) and the 42735A summary do not carry the same content, and thermal figures have been added to megaAVR datasheets over time.
- Do not mix device grades. The 7810D automotive datasheet retrieved here is a different document for a different qualification; its ratings are not interchangeable with the industrial ATmega328P-PU/-PN.
- Do not cite the third-party "junction temperature -55 to 125 °C" line. It is not Microchip's wording, and it most likely restates the operating-temperature absolute-maximum range under a different name.
- When the real theta-JA is obtained, re-run section 5 with it and with the datasheet's stated test condition; if the condition is a JEDEC 4-layer board and the product is a 2-layer board, derate the figure upward (a 2-layer board typically runs materially hotter) before using it.

blocked_on.why: Ask 2 (junction-to-ambient thermal resistance in degC/W, ATmega328P, 28-pin PDIP, from DS40002061B): the retrieved grounding contains no thermal-characteristics table and no theta-JA value for any package. The Microchip product-page fetches returned only navigation/chatbot boilerplate; the 7810D automotive PDF passages cover pinout, memory map and TWI; the Atmel-42735A summary is a 16-page ordering/pinout summary with no electrical or thermal characteristics. No verifiable number exists to report, and ask 1 forbids substituting another revision, another document, or a generic package value.

Ask 3 (maximum junction temperature or total power dissipation specified in DS40002061B): neither parameter appears anywhere in the grounding. The only related third-party claim (circuitbase.tech: 'Junction temperature -55 to 125 C') is not from Microchip, appears to relabel the datasheet's operating-temperature absolute-maximum line, and cannot be cited as the datasheet's junction-temperature or power-dissipation rating.

5.2.7. AVCC
AVCC is the supply voltage pin for the A/D Converter, PC[3:0], and PE[3:2]. It should be externally
connected to VCC, even if the ADC is not used. If the ADC is used, it should be connected to VCC through
a low-pass filter. Note that PC[6:4] use digital supply voltage, VCC.
5.2.8. AREF
AREF is the analog reference pin for the A/D Converter.
